skill.name: set-up-magento-google-ads-ltv-bidding
skill.description: LTV (customer lifetime value) bidding for Magento (Adobe Commerce) in Google Ads. Use this skill when a Magento merchant wants Google Ads to value customers by what they spend over time: LTV or CLV bidding, or value-based bidding for repeat buyers. With every paid order it sends the customer's lifetime revenue and profit, so the campaign bids on customers who come back. It works through Product Metrics, so use it even when Product Metrics is never mentioned. The Magento module is installed by a developer. Not for POAS, new customer or returning customer bidding: each has its own skill, as do other store platforms and ad channels.
skill.summary: Use Product Metrics to verify Magento lifetime value tracking and plan a Google Ads bidding rollout.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts matched Markdown, documentation, or routine setup checks. The guide introduces third-party package trust and permits authenticated remote operations without a general approval rule. Other risks include out-of-scope ad connections, unnecessary order-data access, and unverified browser handoffs; no audit-directed prompt injection or covert data transfer was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer and skill to verified versions or revisions. Restrict the Composer repository to Product Metrics packages and verify package integrity before deploying.

remediation.issue: Authenticated remote operations lack a general approval rule
remediation.suggestion: Use read-only access by default. Require approval for each write after showing the action, workspace, property, affected account, and expected effect.

remediation.issue: Google Ads setup may expand to other ad channels
remediation.suggestion: Use a Google Ads-only checklist for this skill. Present other channels as opt-in and explain the data they would receive before requesting separate approval.

remediation.issue: Order checks can read more customer data than necessary
remediation.suggestion: Ask for a test order reference and a confirmed store view. Return only the tracking status and required metrics, without customer identifiers.

remediation.issue: Browser handoffs do not require destination verification
remediation.suggestion: Accept only expected HTTPS origins and paths for each setup step. Check redirect destinations and warn the user before presenting an unexpected link.

content.user_title: Set Up Magento LTV Bidding in Google Ads
content.value_statement: First-purchase revenue can understate the value of repeat buyers. Use Product Metrics to verify Magento lifetime value tracking and prepare a Google Ads bidding change.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status and identify incomplete Magento or Google Ads steps.
Guide verification of Revenue LTV and Profit LTV conversion actions while they are secondary.
Check whether a paid test order arrived and whether Product Metrics recognized the customer.
Explain the consent, customer matching, and cost requirements for LTV signals.
Guide a one-campaign rollout and read back conversion action status after the account owner makes the change.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, an authorized workspace, and a connected Google Ads account and Merchant Center.
A developer must install the Magento module and keep scheduled jobs running.
LTV uses observed orders after connection and tracks customers separately by store view. It does not predict future purchases.
Profit LTV needs known costs. The account owner must make campaign bidding changes in Google Ads.

use_cases.title: Check Readiness
use_cases.description: Identify missing setup steps before adopting lifetime value bidding for a Magento store.

use_cases.title: Plan a Campaign Pilot
use_cases.description: Choose a revenue or profit signal and prepare a target ROAS for one campaign.

use_cases.title: Validate Store Tracking
use_cases.description: Use a paid test order to check store view routing, order delivery, and customer recognition.

prompt_templates.title: Explain LTV Bidding
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn the basics before connecting any accounts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain Revenue LTV and Profit LTV for Magento. Tell me what I need before setup. Do not connect to any account.

prompt_templates.title: Review Setup Status
prompt_templates.scenario: Check an authorized workspace without changing settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup for workspace [workspace] and store view [store view]. List the missing Google Ads prerequisites. Make no changes.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Paid Test Order
prompt_templates.scenario: Check tracking before changing the primary conversion action.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether paid test order [test order reference] arrived for [store view]. Report recognition and cost availability without showing customer identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a One-Campaign Rollout
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a campaign change for account owner approval.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the LTV actions for [Google Ads account]. Recommend a primary signal and target ROAS for [campaign]. List the manual steps without making changes.

output_examples.input: Check whether the default Magento store view is ready for LTV bidding.
output: The Magento connection is active. Google Ads Data Manager access still needs approval.
Approve access in Google Ads, then confirm the LTV actions exist as secondary.

output_examples.input: Check whether my paid test order supports Profit LTV.
output: Product Metrics received the test order and recognized the customer.
Revenue was recorded. A missing item cost prevents Profit LTV for this order.

output_examples.input: Prepare an LTV rollout for one campaign.
output: Start with Revenue LTV because profit costs are incomplete.
Keep one purchase action primary for the pilot. Set a target ROAS based on the new signal.

best_practices: Confirm the workspace, store view, and Google Ads client account before checking setup or requesting any change.
Verify consent and test tracking with an authorized order. Report only the details needed for the check.
Pilot one campaign and keep one purchase action primary for its bidding goal.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse a purchase action target ROAS without reviewing LTV signal coverage and values.
Do not make Revenue LTV and Profit LTV primary together for the same bidding goal.
Do not paste Magento configuration files, tokens, or customer identifiers into assistant chats.

faq.question: Do I need a Magento developer?
faq.answer: Yes. A developer installs the Product Metrics module and verifies that Magento scheduled jobs can run.

faq.question: Does LTV include orders placed before setup?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics counts paid orders it observes after the store view is connected.

faq.question: How does each order contribute to LTV?
faq.answer: An eligible conversion carries only what that order adds to the customer's lifetime value, not the running total.

faq.question: Why is Profit LTV missing?
faq.answer: Profit LTV requires known costs. Check Magento item costs, order currency, and additional costs in Product Metrics.

faq.question: What consent is required for an LTV conversion?
faq.answer: The visitor must allow analytics and ad user data. Google Ads also needs eligible customer details to match the order.

faq.question: Who makes a conversion action primary?
faq.answer: The Google Ads account owner makes the change. The assistant can explain the steps and verify the resulting status.
